But that signal alone does NOT mean the work failed — the bead can be **complete-but-stuck-open**, typically because prior `br close` attempts silently failed (see [[auto-dispatch-br-close-body-invalid]] and [[br-close-claimed-at-rfc3339]]). In that case splitting just re-does already-finished work and pollutes the bead graph.\n12\t\n13\t**Concrete case (bf-34lwt, 2026-07-07):** Auto-split fired asking to re-investigate a REJECT/token root cause. It was stuck open only because the templated `br close --body` kept failing. `br close bf-34lwt` (no flags) closed it instantly and broke the loop.\n14\t\n15\t**How to apply — before honoring an Auto-Split dispatch, check whether the work is already done:**\n16\t1. `br comments list <parent-of-this-bead>` — is the deliverable already posted?\n17\t2. `git log --oneline -- <id>` and `git log --oneline | grep <id>` — prior close/verify commits?\n18\t3. Are its existing children already `closed` (`br show <each>`)?\n19\t4. Does the committed artifact exist?\n20\t\n21\tIf the work is verifiably complete: post a \"already done, closing to break stuck-close loop\" comment, then `br close <id>` (no `--body`), then `br sync --flush-only`. Do NOT split. Do NOT emit `SPLIT_COMPLETE`. If genuinely incomplete, then split per the dispatch.\n22\t\n23\t**Concrete case (bf-4mle6, 2026-07-07) — the OTHER branch (genuinely incomplete, so DO split, but scope to gaps):** Auto-split fired on a bead with 372 lines of *uncommitted* implementation in the working tree (`cmd/sim/main.go` provisioning real tokens via `/api/provision`) — but its acceptance criteria were NOT met: PROGRESS.md still described the now-obsolete old policy, nothing verified behavior under `SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0`, and the e2e diff was *mixed* with unrelated bf-4q5w (IO-6 hard-gate) test code. **How to apply when incomplete-but-already-implemented:** split into children scoped to the REMAINING GAPS (verify the claim → fix/test the harness → document+commit+close), and put \"the implementation ALREADY EXISTS in the working tree — do NOT re-implement\" at the top of the first child so no child re-does written code. Add a child to DISENTANGLE unrelated work mixed into the same diff (it belongs to a different bead — keep it out of this bead's commit/acceptance). Don't close incomplete/uncommitted work; the \"failures\" are usually the stuck-close symptom, not a sign the task is too big.\n24\t\n25\t**THIRD branch — failure-count from TIMEOUTS, not incompleteness (bf-20q9o, 2026-07-07):** Auto-split fired on a broad *diagnostic* bead (\"pin where sim CSI is dropped in the fusion path\") at failure-count:3. But the metadata in `.beads/traces/bf-20q9o/metadata.json` showed all 3 \"failures\" were `exit_code:124, outcome:timeout, duration_ms:600001` — the agent kept hitting the 10-min ceiling mid-investigation, NOT failing the task. The 10MB `stdout.txt` trace held a **near-complete root-cause finding** the prior run had reached but never posted (it timed out one verification away). **How to apply when failures are timeouts on a diagnostic/research bead:** before splitting, (1) read `metadata.json` — if `outcome:timeout`, the prior run may have the answer; (2) parse the trace's `text_delta` (assistant visible text) and `tool_result`/`file_path` entries with a small python json-stream reader (NOT thinking deltas — those are noise); (3) if a concrete finding exists, **verify it at HEAD yourself** (don't trust the trace secondhand — re-Read the cited `file:line`), then post it as a comment + `br close` (no `--body`). Splitting would discard a 90%-done diagnosis and fragment a solved problem across children that would just re-derive what the trace already holds. For bf-20q9o the trace's finding (colon-vs-dash delimiter mismatch between `CSIFrame.LinkID()` frame.go:119-121 and `splitLinkID` main.go:5407-5415) verified clean at HEAD → posted comment 144 → closed. Is it now `closed`? (2) `git log --oneline | grep <blocker-id>` — did it land recently? All 3 acceptance criteria met by existing code → posted FUSE-DBG evidence as comment + `br close` (no --body) → closed. Splitting would have fabricated 5 children for a task that was already done the moment its blocker landed. **Distinguishing this branch:** the diagnostic is *temporal* — were the failures during a period when a named dependency was still open? If so, re-run the now-unblocked task before trusting failure-count as a complexity measure. When Auto-Split fires on a child whose title is \"commit and close <parent>\", check the working tree FIRST: if the deliverable is already written (especially a PROGRESS.md/doc change), commit the focused set (using explicit paths so unrelated beads' diffs stay out) and close — do NOT split, do NOT emit SPLIT_COMPLETE.
